title: Supporting the bereaved - Death of a loved one

body.value:
This page will guide you through the legal requirements that need to be fulfilled from the moment someone dies in Ireland.

It also directs you to guidance on what to do when an Irish citizen dies while abroad.

Expected death

If the death occurs at home or elsewhere, such as a hospital or nursing home, a doctor must be contacted to confirm the death and issue a Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCDD). This certificate is ordered by the registered medical practitioner.

If the death occurs in a hospital or nursing home, staff usually handle first steps and contact the family.

The MCDD is given to a relative or civil partner of the deceased, or if there are none, to another qualified informant.

Access a list of qualified informants.

Sudden or unexpected death

If the death is sudden or unexpected, An Garda Síochána and the Coroner must be notified.

Death of an Irish citizen abroad

Where an Irish citizen dies abroad and they were ordinarily resident in Ireland within 5 years of their death, it is possible to have the death recorded in the record of deaths abroad.

Funeral directors are usually contacted soon after the death occurs. They can help collect the body once legally permitted.

They also guide the family through:

  • transport of the deceased
  • care and preparation of the body
  • choosing burial versus cremation
  • planning the funeral service

It is a legal requirement to register the death within three months, but this is usually done much sooner.

The death must be registered at a local Civil Registration Office (CRO).

Make an appointment at the CRO through the HSE.

You need:

  • the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (MCCD)
  • personal details (full name, date of birth, PPS number, occupation, marital status)

You receive a Death Certificate, which is needed for probate, pensions, banks, and insurance.

While it is free to register a death, ordering a death certificate costs €20.

Order a death certificate online.

You can also order one from the General Register Office by downloading and emailing the below form to GROonlinepayments@welfare.ie.

Application for certificate of Birth/Death/Marriage/Adoption/Civil Partnership (by email)

More information on ordering certificates.

After the funeral, you need to notify the relevant institutions, such as banks, insurance companies and Revenue connected to the person who has died.

You need to do this so you can:

  • stop or transfer pensions and benefits
  • close or transfer utilities, property matters and tenancy agreements

An executor or solicitor handles the estate.

If no will exists, the estate is distributed under intestacy law.
